questions.q: Which of these best defines an embedded system?
options: A computer built into a larger device to carry out a dedicated function
A computer that can run any program the user installs
A computer with no processor of its own
A computer that is connected to the internet at all times
questions.feedback: Built in, and dedicated to one job. That is what separates it from a general-purpose computer.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.1 Lesson 4 — Smart home, station 1: What is an embedded system?

questions.q: State what is meant by a dedicated function.

markPoints.concept: it does one job, or a small fixed set of jobs

questions.example: It carries out one particular job, rather than any program the user chooses.
questions.paraphrase: It only performs a single specific task.
questions.feedback: One job. A washing machine controller will never be asked to edit a photograph.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.1 Lesson 4 — Smart home, station 1: What is an embedded system?

questions.q: Which of these contain an embedded system? Tick all that apply.
options: A microwave oven
A set of traffic lights
A fitness tracker
A desktop PC running Windows
A paper notebook
questions.feedback: A desktop PC is general purpose: it runs whatever you install. A notebook has no computer in it at all.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.1 Lesson 4 — Smart home, station 1: What is an embedded system?

questions.q: Which are typical characteristics of an embedded system? Tick all that apply.
options: It runs one dedicated program
It usually uses little power
It is often cheap to mass produce
It is designed to be very reliable
It lets the user install new applications
It always has a large colour screen
correct: It is often cheap to mass produce
It is designed to be very reliable
questions.feedback: Dedicated, low power, cheap, reliable. Installing applications is what a general-purpose computer is for.

questions.q: Explain why an embedded system is usually designed to be very reliable.

markPoints.concept: it is built into a device and often cannot easily be repaired or restarted by the user
accept: cannot be repaired|cannot repair|cannot easily repair|cannot be fixed|cannot fix|cannot restart|cannot be restarted|cannot be replaced|cannot be accessed|cannot access|cannot reach|cannot be serviced|not easy to repair|hard to repair|difficult to repair|not be repaired|not be replaced|no way to repair
markPoints.exemplar: It is built into the device, so the user cannot easily repair or restart it.

markPoints.concept: and a failure may be dangerous or stop the whole device working
accept: whole device|entire device|whole product|whole machine|whole thing|useless|unusable|stop working|stops working|would fail|no longer works|breaks down
markPoints.exemplar: If it failed, the whole device would stop working, and in something like a car's brakes that could be dangerous.

questions.example: An embedded system is built into the device, so a user cannot easily repair or restart it, and if it failed the whole device would stop working — which in something safety-critical such as anti-lock brakes could be dangerous.
questions.paraphrase: Because it is inside the product the owner cannot fix it, so a fault would make the whole thing unusable or even unsafe.
questions.feedback: Two different reasons are acceptable; the second mark is for a consequence rather than a restatement.

questions.q: Sort each device by whether its computer is embedded or general purpose.
questions.feedback: A smartwatch is a borderline case worth thinking about: it runs apps, but it is built into one device for a fixed set of jobs, so it is normally treated as embedded.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.1 Lesson 4 — Smart home, station 3: Embedded systems everywhere

questions.q: Give one example of an embedded system found in a car.

markPoints.concept: a named car system, such as engine management, anti-lock brakes or automatic lights

questions.feedback: Any dedicated system built into the car. 'The radio' is accepted only if you say it is built in and does one job.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.1 Lesson 4 — Smart home, station 3: Embedded systems everywhere

questions.q: A washing machine is an embedded system. Match each part to its role.
questions.feedback: Sensors in, decisions in the middle, motors and lights out.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.1 Lesson 4 — Smart home, station 4: Input, process, output

questions.q: A smart thermostat keeps a room at 20°C. Describe how it uses input, process and output to do this.

markPoints.concept: input: a temperature sensor measures the room
markPoints.exemplar: A temperature sensor measures how warm the room is.

markPoints.concept: process: the system compares the reading with the target temperature
markPoints.exemplar: It compares that reading with the target of 20 degrees.

markPoints.concept: output: it switches the heating on or off
markPoints.exemplar: It switches the heating on if the room is too cold.

questions.example: A temperature sensor measures the room, which is the input. The microcontroller compares that reading with the target of 20°C, which is the process. If the room is colder it switches the heating on, which is the output.
questions.paraphrase: It reads the room temperature with a sensor, decides whether that is below the set value, and turns the boiler on or off accordingly.
questions.feedback: One mark each, and each needs the actual thing — 'input' on its own is not a sensor.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.1 Lesson 4 — Smart home, station 4: Input, process, output

questions.q: In a set of traffic lights, which of these is the output?
options: The coloured lamps that change
The pressure sensor in the road
The timer inside the controller
The program stored in the controller
questions.feedback: Lamps change state, so they are the output. The sensor is an input and the timer and the program are part of the processing.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.1 Lesson 4 — Smart home, station 4: Input, process, output

questions.q: The program inside an embedded system, stored permanently in the device, is usually called:
options: firmware
an operating system
a utility
a device driver
questions.feedback: Firmware. Some of it can be updated, which is what a smart TV software update is doing.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.1 Lesson 4 — Smart home, station 5: Programming embedded systems

questions.q: Embedded systems are often programmed in a low-level language such as C rather than in Python. Explain one reason why.

markPoints.concept: a low-level language runs faster or uses less memory
accept: fast|quick|speed|rapid|more instruction|more cycle|sooner|less memory|smaller|efficient|efficiency|less space|less power|close to the hardware|fewer instructions
markPoints.exemplar: C runs faster and uses less memory.

markPoints.concept: which matters because an embedded system has limited resources or must respond in real time
accept: real time|real-time|immediately|quickly enough|straight away|respond in time|deadline
markPoints.exemplar: This matters because the device has very little memory and has to respond in real time.

questions.example: C compiles to code that runs faster and needs less memory, which matters because an embedded system has very limited memory and processing power and often has to respond in real time.
questions.paraphrase: Low-level code is more efficient, which matters because these devices have hardly any memory or processing power and must react immediately.
questions.feedback: Efficiency, then why efficiency matters here. The second mark is the one about this kind of device.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.1 Lesson 4 — Smart home, station 5: Programming embedded systems

questions.q: Compare an embedded system with a general-purpose computer.

markPoints.concept: an embedded system has a dedicated function; a general-purpose computer runs many different programs
markPoints.exemplar: An embedded system does one dedicated job, while a general-purpose computer can run many different programs.

markPoints.concept: an embedded system is built into a larger device; a general-purpose computer is a device in its own right
markPoints.exemplar: An embedded system is built into a larger device.

markPoints.concept: an embedded system usually has limited memory, power and processing; a general-purpose computer has far more
markPoints.exemplar: An embedded system has much less memory and processing power.

markPoints.concept: so an embedded system is cheaper and more reliable, but cannot be repurposed
markPoints.exemplar: This means an embedded system is cheaper and more reliable, but it cannot be given a different job.

questions.example: An embedded system carries out one dedicated function and is built into a larger device, while a general-purpose computer is a device in its own right that can run any program installed on it. The embedded system has far less memory and processing power. That makes it cheaper and more reliable, but it cannot be repurposed, whereas a laptop can be given an entirely new job just by installing software.
questions.paraphrase: One is dedicated to a single task and built inside another product; the other is a standalone machine that runs whatever software you install. The dedicated one has much smaller resources, which makes it cheap and dependable but impossible to reuse for something else.
questions.feedback: A comparison needs both sides of each point. Four separate differences, with the last one drawing a consequence.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.1 Lesson 4 — Smart home, station 6: Embedded or general purpose?

questions.q: A smart TV runs apps the owner can install, but it is built into one device for watching television. Why is it a difficult case to classify?
options: It has a dedicated purpose like an embedded system, but can run new programs like a general-purpose computer
It has no processor, so neither definition applies
It is only an embedded system while it is connected to the internet
It cannot be classified until its firmware is updated
questions.feedback: Some modern devices genuinely sit between the two definitions, and an exam answer should say which features point each way.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.1 Lesson 4 — Smart home, station 6: Embedded or general purpose?

questions.q: A school is listing the computers in one classroom. Sort each one.
items: The digital clock on the wall
questions.feedback: If the device does one job and you cannot install anything on it, it is embedded.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.1 Lesson 4 — Smart home, Final challenge: spot the embedded system

questions.q: An embedded controller runs this program on a loop. The water temperature sensor reads 38. What does the controller print?
questions.feedback: 38 is less than 40, so the condition is true and the heater is switched on. This is input, process, output in three lines.
